claims.text: CrFeCoNiX alloys in a single-phase high-entropy solid-solution state form stable, coherent protective oxide layers during oxidative or corrosive exposure above 900 °C.
High configurational entropy produces a uniform distribution of alloying elements in the single-phase alloy.
A uniform elemental distribution promotes synchronized oxidation kinetics.
Synchronized oxidation kinetics drive formation of a homogeneous oxide scale.
Multiphase CrFeCoNiX alloys have uneven elemental distributions.
Uneven elemental distributions in multiphase regions generate differential diffusion and oxidation.
Differential diffusion and oxidation produce heterogeneous oxide formation and mechanical stresses.
Heterogeneous oxide formation and associated mechanical stresses cause oxide cracking or spallation.
Homogeneous cation distribution leads to uniform, congruent oxidation.
Uniform, congruent oxidation forms a continuous, adherent, protective oxide scale.
Under identical exposure conditions, single-phase alloys will maintain more cohesive and adherent oxide scales than multiphase alloys.
Multiphase alloys will develop non-uniform, cracked, or spalled oxide scales under the stated exposure conditions.
Lower-configurational-entropy alloys form less protectively coherent oxide scales than single-phase high-entropy alloys.
The proposed behavior applies across CrFeCoNiX alloys where X is Si, Mn, or Al.
The proposed mechanism is applicable above 900 °C in oxidative or corrosive environments.
The proposed relationship may not hold at lower temperatures or in inert environments because oxidation kinetics are altered.
